frames.label: Using vibration from initial tool contact as a detection method implies the tool is already rubbing or cutting, which...
frames.main_point: Using vibration from initial tool contact as a detection method implies the tool is already rubbing or cutting, which generates heat and other undesirable effects that can harm the operation.
frames.source_quote: That being said, if you're getting vibration from the bit touching a surface, you're also getting heat / rubbing / cutting / other bad things.
frames.subject: vibration during tool contact
frames.thread_title: using a vibration / noise sensor as edge finder in a CNC machine

frames.label: For a base-excited mass–spring–damper system, the transmitted motion to the mass diminishes at high excitation freque...
frames.main_point: For a base-excited mass–spring–damper system, the transmitted motion to the mass diminishes at high excitation frequencies, effectively isolating the mass from the base. At sufficiently high frequency ratios, the mass behaves as if it is nearly disconnected due to the dynamic stiffness dominating the response.
frames.source_quote: Consider a mass attached to a base by a spring and a damper. If the base is shaken then at high frequencies the response of the mass falls off, it is as if there is nothing connecting the mass and the base at high frequency.
frames.subject: base-excited SDOF high-frequency transmissibility
frames.thread_title: Base Driven Tuning Fork Mechanical Response Spectrum

frames.label: With constant base displacement excitation, a structure’s response amplitude remains roughly constant at high frequen...
frames.main_point: With constant base displacement excitation, a structure’s response amplitude remains roughly constant at high frequencies (mass-dominated behavior), except near resonances that couple energy into modes.
frames.source_quote: In other words, for a constant base amplitude, the tip amplitude of your tuning fork will also be approximately constant at high frequencies, except when there is a resonance that affects the motion of the system.
frames.subject: base-displacement excitation high-frequency response
frames.thread_title: Base Driven Tuning Fork Mechanical Response Spectrum

frames.label: For a fixed displacement input, the required excitation force rises with the square of frequency (outside resonances)...
frames.main_point: For a fixed displacement input, the required excitation force rises with the square of frequency (outside resonances), because acceleration scales with ω² for a given amplitude.
frames.source_quote:
Note that if you apply a fixed displacement, the 
excitation force
 will increase for higher frequencies (and except where there is a resonance in the displacement response) it will be approximately proportional to the frequency squared.
frames.subject: force scaling under fixed-displacement excitation
frames.thread_title: Base Driven Tuning Fork Mechanical Response Spectrum

frames.label: Under constant force excitation, displacement amplitude decreases as frequency increases, but will diverge as frequen...
frames.main_point: Under constant force excitation, displacement amplitude decreases as frequency increases, but will diverge as frequency approaches zero if the structure is unconstrained (rigid-body mode).
frames.source_quote:
If you applied a constant 
force
, you would see the displacement falling as the frequency increased, but unless the structure is constrained in some way, the displacement amplitude will increase to infinity as the frequency gets close to zero.
frames.subject: constant-force excitation displacement behavior
frames.thread_title: Base Driven Tuning Fork Mechanical Response Spectrum

frames.label: At excitation frequencies well above a structure’s resonances, inertia dominates and stiffness can be neglected in th...
frames.main_point: At excitation frequencies well above a structure’s resonances, inertia dominates and stiffness can be neglected in the equations of motion, simplifying the response to mass-matrix relations.
frames.source_quote: In that situation the elastic forces are small compared with the inertia forces, so we can ignore the stiffness term in the equation of motion
frames.subject: inertia-dominated high-frequency dynamics
frames.thread_title: Base Driven Tuning Fork Mechanical Response Spectrum

frames.label: Vibration and chatter can occur when the cutting/excitation frequency aligns with the system’s natural frequency, lea...
frames.main_point: Vibration and chatter can occur when the cutting/excitation frequency aligns with the system’s natural frequency, leading to resonance and oscillations. This is a dynamics issue rather than a simple tool-wear problem.
frames.source_quote: it might be  that you are operating at a frequency which favours resonance  and oscillations.
frames.subject: machining-induced resonance from excitation frequency
frames.thread_title: Chamfering with a conical bit makes a table drill vibrate

frames.label: Adjust spindle speed up or down to move the excitation away from resonance and reduce vibration
frames.main_point: Adjust spindle speed up or down to move the excitation away from resonance and reduce vibration. Try both higher and lower RPM to find a speed band with less chatter.
frames.source_quote: Can you try increasing the rpms or lowering it and see if the vibrations are less?
frames.subject: spindle speed adjustment to avoid resonance
frames.thread_title: Chamfering with a conical bit makes a table drill vibrate

frames.label: Increase the mass of the workholding/structure (e.g., clamp on an inertia block or a heavy vice) to lower the system’...
frames.main_point: Increase the mass of the workholding/structure (e.g., clamp on an inertia block or a heavy vice) to lower the system’s natural frequency. Shifting the natural frequency can move the system away from resonance and mitigate vibration.
frames.source_quote: If that is the case you can attach some more mass (with a vice ) on the plate  (an inertia block if you like) to lower the natural frequency.
frames.subject: adding mass to shift natural frequency
frames.thread_title: Chamfering with a conical bit makes a table drill vibrate

frames.label: If the support post’s natural frequency aligns with the pipe’s vibration, resonance can amplify motion and corrupt me...
frames.main_point: If the support post’s natural frequency aligns with the pipe’s vibration, resonance can amplify motion and corrupt measurements. Avoid frequency overlap to prevent instrument reading errors.
frames.source_quote: But the vibration of your hot pipe could resonate with that of the post and throw all the readings off.
frames.subject: resonance between pipe and support post
frames.thread_title: Help with designing support structures for instrument

frames.label: Identify the pipe/support system’s natural frequency and design the instrument post so its natural frequency is suffi...
frames.main_point: Identify the pipe/support system’s natural frequency and design the instrument post so its natural frequency is sufficiently separated to avoid resonance with the pipe.
frames.source_quote: so we need more information about your pipe section, its supports, and the natural frequency of those to design the post with a natural frequency away from that.
frames.subject: support natural frequency separation from source vibrations
frames.thread_title: Help with designing support structures for instrument

frames.label: An abrupt, step-like change in applied force will excite a mechanical system’s natural modes, producing ringing or os...
frames.main_point: An abrupt, step-like change in applied force will excite a mechanical system’s natural modes, producing ringing or oscillations. This is a fundamental response to discontinuous inputs in dynamic systems.
frames.source_quote: In theory, an instantaneous change in force will also excite natural vibrations in a system as well (in the same way connecting an inductor/capacitor directly to a 12v source induces ringing).
frames.subject: natural vibration excitation from instantaneous force change
